[rebellion:impl.engine-scope] What the core-v1 engine can do: The engine plays only the Command Phase: on a turn a side activates a system with a leader from its pool, moves its own units into it, finishes the activation, or passes. Where a game tracks cards, the Empire draws 2 probe cards in each Refresh while the deck lasts; no other rules for probe droids exist. Combat, missions, production, deployment, recruiting, other card mechanics, objectives, loyalty and subjugation are not implemented: rules about them do not apply, and only the actions listed by the engine exist. (RR p.2; RR p.3)
[rebellion:base.reveal-condition] When the Rebel base must be revealed: Whenever the Empire has loyalty or ground units in the Rebel base's system, the Rebel player must reveal the base. The condition is checked at any time, not only after movement. (RR p.11; LTP p.12)
[rebellion:base.reveal-timing] Revealing the base after Imperial ground units move in: When Imperial ground units move into a system, the Rebel player must declare whether his base is there; if so, it is revealed after all movement of the activation and before combat. (RR p.2; RR p.11; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.activate.place-leader] Activate a system by placing a leader: To activate a system the player takes one leader from his own leader pool and places it in any system on the map. Activation is how units move and combats start. (RR p.2; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.activate.steps] Steps of an activation: Five steps: 1 place the leader; 2 move own units in from adjacent systems; 3 reveal the base if Imperial ground units moved into its system; 4 combat if both sides share a theater; 5 subjugate if an Imperial ground unit is in a system without Imperial loyalty. (RR p.2)
[rebellion:command.move.into-activated-from-adjacent] Units move only into the activated system, from adjacent systems: Units move only during an activation and only into the activated system, from any number of systems adjacent to it. Units cannot move into a system that was not activated. (RR p.9; RR p.2; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.move.own-leader-locks] Units cannot leave a system that contains their own leader: Units cannot move out of a system containing a leader of their own faction, even one without tactic values. Leaders placed earlier in the phase stay until Refresh and keep locking their systems. (RR p.9; RR p.2; RR p.8; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.pass] Passing: A player may pass. Then he cannot activate systems or reveal missions for the rest of this Command Phase and his turns are skipped while the other player continues. When both have passed, the Refresh Phase begins. (RR p.6; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.transport.capacity] Transport capacity: Ground units and TIE Fighters move only by transport: each moving ship carries from its own system up to its transport capacity (faction sheet), one place per unit. X-wings and Y-wings need no transport. (RR p.9; RR p.14; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.transport.restriction-icon] Transport restriction icon: Units with the transport restriction icon (ground units, TIE Fighters) move only together with transport-capacity units leaving the same system; ships staying behind or already at the destination cannot carry them. (RR p.9; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.turn-order] Command Phase turn order: The Rebels take the first Command Phase turn, then the players alternate. A turn is activating a system with a pool leader or revealing an assigned mission; instead of a turn a player may pass. (RR p.6; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:round.structure] Game round: Assignment, Command, Refresh: The game is a series of rounds, each with three phases in order: Assignment (leaders go on missions), Command (players alternate turns) and Refresh (cleanup, time advances), until one side wins. (LTP p.6; RR p.13; LTP p.20)
[rebellion:victory.empire] Imperial victory: conquer the revealed base: The Empire wins immediately when the Rebel base is revealed and its system holds at least one Imperial unit (any unit) and no Rebel units. While the base is hidden this cannot happen. (RR p.14; LTP p.11)
[rebellion:victory.rebels] Rebel victory: reputation meets time: The Rebels win immediately when the reputation marker and the time marker are on the same space of the time track. Time advances one space per round; reputation moves toward time when the Rebels gain reputation. (RR p.14; RR p.12; LTP p.11)
[rebellion:command.activate.system-with-leader] A system that already holds a leader can be activated: A player may activate a system that already contains a leader. (RR p.2)
[rebellion:command.activate.tactic-values-required] Only leaders with tactic values can activate: A leader that has no tactic values cannot be used to activate a system. Such a leader still stops its own side's units from leaving the system it stands in. (RR p.2; RR p.9; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:base.death-star-does-not-reveal] The Death Star does not reveal the base: A Death Star or Death Star Under Construction in the same system as the hidden base does not reveal it: ships, including the Death Star, never reveal the base; only Imperial ground units or Imperial loyalty in the base's system do (RR p.11). (FAQ p.1; RR p.11)

[rebellion:command.transport.capacity] Transport capacity: Ground units and TIE Fighters move only by transport: each moving ship carries from its own system up to its transport capacity (faction sheet), one place per unit. X-wings and Y-wings need no transport. (RR p.9; RR p.14; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.transport.restriction-icon] Transport restriction icon: Units with the transport restriction icon (ground units, TIE Fighters) move only together with transport-capacity units leaving the same system; ships staying behind or already at the destination cannot carry them. (RR p.9; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:command.turn-order] Command Phase turn order: The Rebels take the first Command Phase turn, then the players alternate. A turn is activating a system with a pool leader or revealing an assigned mission; instead of a turn a player may pass. (RR p.6; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:round.structure] Game round: Assignment, Command, Refresh: The game is a series of rounds, each with three phases in order: Assignment (leaders go on missions), Command (players alternate turns) and Refresh (cleanup, time advances), until one side wins. (LTP p.6; RR p.13; LTP p.20)
[rebellion:victory.empire] Imperial victory: conquer the revealed base: The Empire wins immediately when the Rebel base is revealed and its system holds at least one Imperial unit (any unit) and no Rebel units. While the base is hidden this cannot happen. (RR p.14; LTP p.11)
[rebellion:victory.rebels] Rebel victory: reputation meets time: The Rebels win immediately when the reputation marker and the time marker are on the same space of the time track. Time advances one space per round; reputation moves toward time when the Rebels gain reputation. (RR p.14; RR p.12; LTP p.11)
[rebellion:command.activate.system-with-leader] A system that already holds a leader can be activated: A player may activate a system that already contains a leader. (RR p.2)
[rebellion:command.activate.tactic-values-required] Only leaders with tactic values can activate: A leader that has no tactic values cannot be used to activate a system. Such a leader still stops its own side's units from leaving the system it stands in. (RR p.2; RR p.9; LTP p.7)
[rebellion:base.reveal-procedure] How the base is revealed: To reveal, the Rebel player turns the probe card from the "Location" space faceup and puts it on the "Rebel Base" space, where it stays as a reminder. All units and leaders on the "Rebel Base" space are placed in the system shown on that card. (RR p.11; LTP p.12)
[rebellion:command.pass-is-not-action] Passing replaces a turn: Passing is not an action: a player passes instead of taking his turn. (FAQ p.5)
